title: Sacred Geometry
author: Unknown
description: Sacred Geometry, an illustrated text on the symbolic geometry used in religious art, architecture and esoteric cosmology. It begins with the point (circular, or in three dimensions spherical) as the abstract seed of all form, and builds through line, circle and vesica piscis to the classic figures of sacred geometry. It treats Metatron's Cube and the five Platonic solids (tetrahedron, cube or hexahedron, octahedron, dodecahedron and icosahedron) and their traditional association with the elements and the cosmos, along with related forms such as the Flower and Seed of Life, the golden ratio and harmonic proportion. The author is not identified in the file. The work serves as a concise visual primer connecting Pythagorean and Platonic number mysticism with modern sacred-geometry practice, and sits alongside Plato's Timaeus, Kepler and Pacioli in the library.
